name: right-red
title: Red Has to Be the Right Red
kicker: A failing run only counts if it fails for the right reason
html:
Red Has to Be the Right Red

Red, but Not Evidence

It didn’t compile, or the step didn’t exist yet. Something is missing, but not necessarily the behavior.

Every Run Through the Runner

A raw test command is blocked: it would leave nothing in the log.

One Line per Run

Pass or fail, total, failures, errors. No results at all is logged as a failure, reason=no-results.

Then Check It

The right module, failing on behavior, with a plausible total, before any production write.

gate-bash.sh bdd-run-logging.gradle.kts

The log, in order 
1795… FEATURE_WRITE heart/…/options.feature
1795… BDD_RUN FAIL total=412 failures=3 errors=0
1795… MAIN_WRITE heart/…/ActPipeline.kt
1795… BDD_RUN PASS total=412 failures=0 errors=0

The log’s own line kinds; the paths and counts are illustrative.
say: Here's a trap I fell into more than once. A model is told to write the scenario first and watch it fail. It writes the scenario, runs the suite, and the suite fails. Red. Done? Probably not. It failed because the code didn't compile, or because the step it needed didn't exist yet. That's red, but it isn't evidence that the behavior is missing. It's evidence that something is missing. So the skill is strict about what a run is. Tests run only through the skill's own runner; a raw test command is blocked, because a raw run leaves nothing in the log. Every run appends one line: pass or fail, the total, the failures, the errors. A run that produced no results at all is logged as a failure with the reason no-results, so it can't pass for a real red. And I hold one rule on top of the skill: after every red run, before any production write, check that the failure is the right module, on behavior, with a total that makes sense. Notice that it's the same idea as the whole talk: don't trust that the agent did the right thing; make it leave a record you can check.

deck:ref.name: right-behavior
deck:ref.label: RIGHT-BEHAVIOR
deck:ref.title: Right behavior: only what the state allows, and a reason when not
deck:ref.summary: The agent is offered only the acts the current state allows, sends each one with the validator from the state it read, and gets a reason when an act is absent. At the small scale it is a Gherkin scenario that says what right means before any code is written.

deck:fragment.name: bash-gate
deck:fragment.label: Raw test commands are blocked (core/gate-bash.sh)
deck:fragment.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# PreToolUse (Bash). For wrapper-logged stacks: blocks running the raw test
# command, because a raw run leaves no BDD_RUN fact and the pre-commit check
# then cannot see the red/green sequence. No-op unless bddRawCommandRegex is set.
set -o pipefail
. "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"

bdd_has_config || exit 0
regex=$(bdd_value bddRawCommandRegex)
[ -n "$regex" ] || exit 0

command=$(jq -r '.tool_input.command // empty')
[ -n "$command" ] || exit 0
case "$command" in *bdd-gates/bdd-run.sh*) exit 0 ;; esac

if printf '%s\n' "$command" | grep -Eq -- "$regex"; then
  echo "Blocked: run tests through .claude/bdd-gates/bdd-run.sh [extra args] so the BDD_RUN result is logged." >&2
  exit 2
fi
exit 0
